px4.AXES_HINT: Choose on the ground: parameters cannot be written while armed. One axis per flight takes longer, but a tune that misbehaves is easier to abort.
MC_RATE_SECTIONS: Proportional gain on the rate error. Raise until the axis feels crisp, back off before it buzzes.
Integral gain. Removes steady-state error (wind, an off-centre payload) and is what a slow drift back to level comes from.
Derivative gain. Damps overshoot; too much of it amplifies motor and frame noise into heat.
Feed-forward from the rate setpoint. Improves tracking without touching the loop's stability.
Overall gain multiplier for this axis. Scales P, I and D together, so it is the one knob to turn after a payload change.
Ceiling on the integrator, in normalised torque. Stops a long-held error from winding up into a lurch when the vehicle is released.

MC_ATTITUDE_SECTIONS: Turns a roll angle error into a roll rate setpoint. Higher is sharper; too high and the rate loop is asked for more than the airframe can give.
Pitch angle error to pitch rate setpoint.
Heading error to yaw rate setpoint.
How much yaw authority may be taken from roll and pitch when the mixer saturates. Lower keeps the vehicle upright at the cost of heading.
Ceiling on the rate setpoint the attitude loop may request.
MC_VELOCITY_SECTIONS: Horizontal velocity error to acceleration setpoint.
Trims out a steady wind. Too high and the vehicle circles its hold point.
Damps the velocity loop. Sensitive to position noise, so raise it slowly.
Vertical velocity error to acceleration setpoint.
Carries the hover thrust. This is the gain that holds altitude when the battery sags.
Caps the lean angle the velocity loop may ask for, and with it the horizontal acceleration the vehicle can produce.
The throttle that holds a hover. A wrong value makes every altitude change start with a lurch.
MC_POSITION_SECTIONS: Horizontal position error to velocity setpoint. Raise for a tighter hold, lower if the vehicle hunts around its hold point.
How abruptly acceleration may change. Lower is smoother and gentler on a camera; higher tracks a mission leg more tightly.

FW_ATTITUDE_SECTIONS: How quickly the aircraft is asked to reach a commanded roll angle. Smaller is sharper; a large airframe needs a larger value.
AUTOTUNE_STEPS: Fly somewhere open, with room to drift, and keep a hand on the sticks.
Take off and hold a stable hover in Position or Altitude mode, 3-10 m up.
Start the tune and let go of the sticks. The autopilot injects its own steps and needs a clean response to measure.
Expect roughly a minute of visible twitching, one axis at a time.
Land and disarm to apply the gains, then test them gently before flying the aircraft normally.
MC_AUTOTUNE_FIELDS: How hard the autotune shakes the vehicle. Raise it on a large or heavy airframe whose response is otherwise lost in the noise; lower it if the aircraft feels alarming during the tune.
The closed-loop response the tune aims for. Smaller means sharper and hotter motors.
FW_AUTOTUNE_FIELDS: How hard the autotune excites each axis.
Lets the tune be triggered from the transmitter instead of the ground station.
px4.AUTOTUNE_RUNNING_TEXT: The autopilot is exciting each axis in turn and measuring the response. Keep your hands off the sticks and hold the hover. Stop the tune at any time if the vehicle misbehaves.
px4.TUNE_NONE_TEXT: This firmware has no autotune. Set the gains by hand below, on the ground.

APPLY_DONE_TEXT.0: The tune finished. The gains were not applied because the apply setting is Never, so nothing on the vehicle has changed.
APPLY_DONE_TEXT.1: The tune finished. Land and disarm to apply the new gains, then test them gently before flying normally.
APPLY_DONE_TEXT.2: The tune finished and the new gains are already active. Test them gently before flying normally.

COPTER_RATE_SECTIONS: The main gain: how hard the controller reacts to a rate error. Raise it until the aircraft feels crisp, back off at the first sign of a twitch.
Removes steady error: a persistent lean from an off-centre payload or a bent arm. On ArduPilot this normally tracks P.
Damps the response. Too much amplifies motor and frame noise into heat.
Ceiling on the integrator's share of the output, as a fraction of full authority.
Passes the rate setpoint straight through, ahead of the error loop.
Low-pass on the setpoint entering the loop.
Low-pass on the rate error. Lowering it calms a noisy airframe at the cost of response.
Low-pass on the D term specifically, and the usual first thing to lower when a tune makes the motors hot.
Caps how fast the output may move, which is ArduPilot's own guard against a gain that is too high for the airframe. 0 disables it.

COPTER_ATTITUDE_SECTIONS: Turns a roll angle error into a roll rate setpoint. Higher is sharper; too high and the rate loop is asked for more than the airframe can give.
Pitch angle error to pitch rate setpoint.
Heading error to yaw rate setpoint.
How sharply the aircraft answers the sticks. Smaller is more direct.
Centidegrees per second squared, ArduPilot's own unit.
Fastest heading change an automatic mode may command.
How much authority attitude control keeps when the throttle is low. Raising it helps a heavy aircraft stay upright in a fast descent.
COPTER_VELOCITY_SECTIONS: The throttle loop. On most airframes this is the one gain that has to change with a large weight difference.
COPTER_POSITION_SECTIONS: Position error to velocity demand. Raising it makes the aircraft hold a point harder and overshoot a waypoint more.
How abruptly the demanded acceleration may change. Lower is smoother and slower to react.
PLANE_RATE_SECTIONS: The dominant term on a fixed wing: control surfaces are fast enough that most of the demand can go straight through.
How much rudder follows aileron, to keep a turn coordinated.
PLANE_ATTITUDE_SECTIONS: How tightly the aircraft tracks a line between waypoints. Lower turns harder and can weave; higher is smooth and cuts corners.
How quickly the total-energy controller trades speed for height.
COPTER_AUTOTUNE_FIELDS: How much bounce-back the tune accepts before it stops raising a gain. 0.05 is gentle, 0.10 is sharp; 0.075 is the default and suits most airframes.
Floor on the D term, so the tune cannot leave an axis undamped.
PLANE_AUTOTUNE_FIELDS: 1 is very soft, 10 is very sharp. 6 is the default and is a reasonable first flight for most airframes.
COPTER_AUTOTUNE_STEPS: Fly somewhere open and calm. The tune needs room to drift and is thrown off by wind.
Take off and hold a stable hover in Loiter or AltHold, 5-10 m up.
Start the tune. Corvus switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE mode; ArduPilot takes the sticks from there.
Let go of the sticks. Expect visible twitching, one axis at a time, for several minutes. Nudging a stick pauses the tune, it does not break it.
When ArduPilot reports the tune is complete, land with the throttle down and leave the mode switch in AUTOTUNE to keep the new gains, then disarm.
Switching out of AUTOTUNE before landing discards the result; test the new gains gently before flying the aircraft normally.
PLANE_AUTOTUNE_STEPS: Fly somewhere open, in calm air, with plenty of altitude.
Trim the aircraft in FBWA so it flies straight and level hands-off.
Start the tune. Corvus switches the vehicle into AUTOTUNE mode.
Fly it: the plane tunes from your own stick inputs, so give it full aileron and elevator rolls and pitches for a few minutes.
Switch out of AUTOTUNE when the response feels right. The gains are saved as they are learned.
ardupilot.COPTER_RUNNING_TEXT: ArduPilot is tuning in AUTOTUNE mode, one axis at a time, and reports progress in the console rather than as a percentage. Keep the sticks centred: a nudge only pauses the tune. When the console says it is complete, land with the mode still AUTOTUNE and disarm to keep the gains.
ardupilot.PLANE_RUNNING_TEXT: ArduPilot is learning in AUTOTUNE mode from your own stick inputs and reports in the console rather than as a percentage. Fly full roll and pitch movements. The gains are saved as they are learned; switch out of AUTOTUNE when the response feels right.
